clue.text: Patient man meet to seek employment

parts.note: Job is the biblical figure famed for his patience
a meet is a gathering of riders and hounds for a hunt

explanation.surface: A long-suffering man arranges a meeting in order to look for a job.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'meet' in British country life is the assembly before a fox hunt, so the word stands for the hunt itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking for a job is exactly what a person out hunting for work does.

clue.text: After New Year's Day rubbish is picked up by the caretaker

parts.note: January the first is written JAN I, with I as the Roman one

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking up lifts the word upwards, so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: After the holiday the bin men collect the waste, as the building's caretaker sees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is picked up' turns ROT into TOR, which follows JANI; 'After' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A janitor is the person who looks after a building, a caretaker in British usage.

clue.text: Boring article by attorney involved in a fracas

definitions.note: a tool for boring, given as the activity it performs

indicators.note: the article and the lawyer are wrapped inside the word for a fight

parts.note: a fracas is a noisy fight, a brawl
DA is a District Attorney

explanation.surface: A dull lawyer gets mixed up in a scuffle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' means drilling holes, not dull: it describes the tool. 'involved in' puts A and DA inside BRAWL.
explanation.definitionFit: This small pointed hand tool is used to bore holes in wood.

clue.text: A French lover lacking in chivalry

parts.note: un is French for a
a gallant is a dashing suitor

explanation.surface: A Frenchman known as a lover who behaves without courtesy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being discourteous to women is the opposite of being chivalrous.

clue.text: Cargo consists of old horse in good muscular shape

indicators.note: the horse sits inside the word for fitness

parts.note: muscle tone is firmness of the body
a nag is an elderly or worn-out horse

explanation.surface: A shipment includes an ageing horse that is fit and firm.
explanation.definitionFit: The weight of goods a ship carries is measured in tons, its freight.

clue.text: Leave the bank? Get away!

explanation.surface: A boater is told to cast off and is then sent packing.
explanation.definitionFit: A rower leaves the riverside by shoving the boat out with an oar, and the same phrase is a rude dismissal like 'clear off!'.

clue.text: Irishman goes to mine with a quick, light step

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
Pat (Patrick) is the stock Irishman's name in crosswords

explanation.surface: An Irishman heads off to the colliery, walking briskly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes to' only joins the pieces, PIT and A first, then PAT.
explanation.definitionFit: This echoing sound describes rapid, light footfalls or a racing heartbeat.

clue.text: Polish woman held in

indicators.note: the pronoun for a woman holds the little word in inside it

parts.note: she stands for a woman

explanation.surface: A woman from Poland is detained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is not the nationality: it is the verb to buff up.
explanation.definitionFit: To buff something until it gleams is to make it lustrous.

clue.text: Torment caused by out-of-print papers

parts.note: OP is the bookseller's abbreviation for out of print
the press means the newspapers

explanation.surface: A bookish woe brought on by newspapers no longer printed.
explanation.definitionFit: To crush people under harsh rule is to torment them.

clue.text: Scientist gets a long way over a 24-hour period

parts.note: far means at a great distance
a day lasts twenty-four hours

explanation.surface: A researcher travels a great distance over the course of a day.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Faraday was the English physicist who pioneered electromagnetism.
explanation.definitionFit: Faraday was a nineteenth-century English chemist and physicist.

clue.text: Antigen produced by undiluted alcohol

indicators.note: the answer is made out of the letters of the word Antigen, rearranged

explanation.surface: A biological antigen is apparently made by drinking strong spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced by' signals that the letters of ANTIGEN are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A spirit served straight, with no mixer or water, is neat.

clue.text: Excursionist who suffers a loss of standing

definitions.text: who suffers a loss of standing

explanation.surface: A day-tourist who keeps losing their footing.
explanation.definitionFit: A holidaymaker on a day outing is a tourist of that kind, and one who stumbles and falls is literally someone who trips.

clue.text: Rex is in extremity. Follow?

indicators.note: the abbreviation for king sits inside the word for an end piece

parts.note: a tail is the extreme end of a creature or thing
R is the abbreviation for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king is in desperate straits and asks whether to go along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is in' puts R (Rex, king) inside TAIL. The definition is a verb: to trail someone is to follow them.
explanation.definitionFit: To track or shadow someone from behind is to trail them.

clue.text: Understand how to make an arrest

explanation.surface: A question about the correct procedure for taking a suspect into custody.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to grasp an idea mentally and, of police, to seize a suspect.

clue.text: Free to arrange another tenancy

explanation.surface: A landlord offers a property again, perhaps without charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To let something go is to set it at liberty, and to lease a property again is, split as RE-LEASE, a renewed letting.

clue.text: Try this brew if you are!

definitions.text: Try this brew if you are!

indicators.note: a brew is something mixed up, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: An offer of a drink to anyone parched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brew' signals an anagram of TRY THIS, and the whole clue also says who would want a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in need of a drink is parched, and a brew is just the thing for them.

clue.text: Do routine work to be free of wrinkles

indicators.note: the letters of the words Do routine are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to do humdrum chores to look smooth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' signals an anagram of DO ROUTINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A shirt pressed smooth has had its creases removed, and problems settled are smoothed too.

clue.text: I got into bed-but on one side only

indicators.note: the words I got are placed inside the word for a place to sleep

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone climbs into bed but keeps to one half of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts IGOT inside BED.
explanation.definitionFit: A prejudiced person sees only one side of any argument.

clue.text: Kalahari native who voted Republican last election

definitions.text: Kalahari native who voted Republican last election

parts.words: Kalahari native who voted Republican last election
parts.note: a desert people of southern Africa, with a pun on a supporter of the Republican president George W. Bush

explanation.surface: A southern African desert dweller apparently backed the GOP.
explanation.definitionFit: The San people of the Kalahari were long known by this English name.

clue.text: Grenade manufactured by Iberian bigwig

indicators.note: the letters of the word Grenade are made into something new

explanation.surface: A bomb made by a Spanish nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manufactured' signals an anagram of GRENADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandee is a Spanish or Portuguese nobleman of the highest rank, a VIP.

clue.text: Speckled fruit in divine surroundings

indicators.note: the abbreviation for a theologian goes around the fruit

parts.note: a divine is a clergyman; DD is Doctor of Divinity
an apple is a fruit

explanation.surface: Spotted fruit inside a holy setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divine' is a noun here, a clergyman, abbreviated DD; 'surroundings' puts DD round APPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Marked with spots or patches of colour, like a horse with mottled coat.

clue.text: Ill humour leads to a complaint

parts.note: choler is anger, one of the old four humours (yellow bile)

explanation.surface: Bad temper ends in someone making a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill humour' is a nod to the medieval bodily humours: choler, yellow bile, caused bad temper. 'Complaint' means an illness, not a grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: An illness or disease is called a complaint, and this bacterial infection is one.

clue.text: Put the shutter down to take a photo

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper closes the shop and then takes a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To shut a shop for the night is to close it, and a picture taken from very near is a tight shot.

clue.text: The embodiment of a mince pie, in my opinion

indicators.note: to mince is to chop up, so the word pie is chopped into a new order

parts.note: to me is an informal way to say in my view

explanation.surface: Someone declares a mince pie the perfect example of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mince' looks part of 'mince pie' but is the anagram signal: PIE becomes EPI.
explanation.definitionFit: The perfect example of a quality is its personification.

clue.text: He examines any salt mixture

indicators.note: the letters of the words any salt are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A chemist studies a blend of salts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixture' signals an anagram of ANY SALT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who studies data or substances closely is an examiner.

clue.text: Rise to offer resistance

parts.note: to rise is to get to your feet

explanation.surface: Getting up in order to resist something.
explanation.definitionFit: To confront or defy someone bravely is to resist them.

clue.text: Paper design transferred last month by a novice

parts.note: Dec, December, is the final month of the year
L is a learner, from the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A newcomer moved a paper pattern just a few weeks ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last month' is not 'the previous month' but the final month of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: A transfer picture that slides from backing paper onto a surface is this sticker.

clue.text: Heath gives heart to Americans

indicators.note: the inner letters of the word Americans supply the answer

explanation.surface: A stretch of moorland encourages visitors from the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives heart to' points to the central letters of AMERICANS.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the botanical genus of heathers, so the plant is a heath.

clue.text: Claimed treatment to be therapeutic

indicators.note: treating the word Claimed means working its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A remedy that someone asserted would heal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatment' signals an anagram of CLAIMED.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the healing of illness is what both adjectives describe.

clue.text: Saving a small business beset by money trouble

indicators.note: the business abbreviation is surrounded by the rearranged letters
the word money is troubled, its letters stirred about

parts.note: Co is the short form of company

explanation.surface: A little firm struggling with cash problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' turns MONEY into ENOMY; 'beset by' puts CO inside, after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrift or cutting costs is a form of frugality.

clue.text: Want to be given guidance when provoked

parts.note: to want is to need
someone shown the way is led

explanation.surface: Someone who wants help on being annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be needled is to be irritated or goaded, as by repeated pricks.

clue.text: One in obvious need of TLC

definitions.text: One in obvious need of TLC

parts.words: One in obvious need of TLC
parts.note: TLC, tender loving care, is what a person under medical treatment in a hospital ward most needs

explanation.surface: Someone who plainly needs a bit of looking after.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital case is under care, so needs tender loving care more than anyone.
